seo_title: Copy text from screen on macOS
seo_description: Free, open-source menu bar app for macOS. Press a hotkey, drag over any text on screen, and it is copied to your clipboard using on-device OCR.
hero_sub: Press ⇧⌘2, drag a box over any text on screen, and it lands on your clipboard. Recognition runs on-device with Apple's Vision framework, so nothing leaves your Mac.
features_sub: ScreenTextGrab lives in your menu bar and does a single thing: turn pixels into text you can paste.

features.title: Global rebindable hotkey
features.desc: Start a capture from any app with ⇧⌘2, or record your own shortcut in Settings. An optional second hotkey scans the whole main display.

features.title: On-device text recognition
features.desc: Uses Apple's Vision framework with Accurate or Fast modes, automatic language detection or a language list you choose. If the first pass finds nothing, it retries on the image rotated 90 degrees.

features.title: Clean output you control
features.desc: Results are ordered top to bottom, left to right. Optionally join lines to remove line breaks and trim extra whitespace.

features.title: QR codes and barcodes
features.desc: Turn on code reading and the payload of any QR code or barcode in your selection is copied to the clipboard.

features.title: Recent captures in the menu
features.desc: The last 20 captures are kept in memory only and can be re-copied from the menu. Quit the app and they are gone.

features.title: Private by design
features.desc: No accounts, servers or network calls, and no images written to disk. The app excludes its own windows from the capture.

permissions_step: On your first capture, grant Screen Recording in System Settings → Privacy & Security, then quit and reopen the app.

faq.q: Is ScreenTextGrab really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, with no ads, accounts or paid tier. The full source is on GitHub, and if it saves you time you can optionally support development through the Support / Donate button.

Screen Recording is required, because macOS only lets apps read screen pixels with it. Notifications are optional. It does not ask for Accessibility or Microphone access, since the global hotkey uses the Carbon hot key API.
Only your settings are saved, in macOS UserDefaults. Captured images are processed in memory and released right after recognition, and the Recent Captures list is never written to disk.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to approve it, or build it yourself from source with Xcode and XcodeGen.
